analysis.title: Inside Commodities, November 18, 2026
key_insights: China's October refined fuel exports fell 27.7% from September to 5.18 million tons but rose 14.6% year-on-year. Jan-Oct exports were 46.59 million tons, down 2.0% y/y. Beijing restricted refined product exports in mid-March over Middle East supply risks and eased the curbs in mid-July.

China's October diesel exports were 1.4 million tons, up 89.2% y/y but down from 1.85 million tons in September. Jet fuel exports were 1.48 million tons (-14.0% y/y). Gasoline exports were 540,000 tons (-27.8% y/y).
China's October LNG imports rose 5.0% y/y to 5.53 million tons. Jan-Oct LNG imports were 50.12 million tons, down 4.8% y/y.

Reuters columnist Maguire argues US energy export volumes can still grow, but market-share gains will be much harder to repeat. US LNG has gone from about 5% of global trade in 2018 to over 30% recently. Crude is at roughly 10-15% of global exports, and propane at about two-thirds of world trade.

Rival LNG projects in Qatar, Canada and the UAE will compete for European and Asian buyers. Normalized Middle East oil supply would cut the appeal of US barrels, which carry longer transit times and higher shipping costs. Future US growth depends on demand growth and cost competitiveness rather than geopolitical disruption.

India's rice output rose 50% in a decade to a record 154 million tons in 2025/26 against domestic consumption of 107 million tons. Exports doubled to 22.3 million tons in 2025, about 40% of global rice trade. Government rice stocks hit a record 55.47 million tons on October 1, more than four times target.

Rice subsidies are over two-thirds of India's federal food subsidy bill, which reached 2.28 trillion rupees in 2025/26. Indian rice trades about $110 a ton below Thai benchmark rice, which was around $497 a ton in mid-November. Thailand and Vietnam have complained about price pressure, and the US has accused India of dumping.

Poor El Nino rains are expected to lower India's 2026/27 harvest, but USDA still forecasts higher Indian exports over the next two years because stocks are ample. State bonuses on top of the federal minimum price are resisted by farmers and the federal government has made little headway in stopping them.

Ukraine's agriculture minister says the 2027 grain harvest could halve to 30 million tons from 62 million in 2026 because blocked Black Sea ports make exporting unviable. Corn could fall to 12-14 million tons from 29-30 million. Wheat could fall by more than a third to 17 million tons.

Ukraine's 2026/27 grain exports could fall to 24.6 million tons from 38 million tons if ports stay blocked, and could rebound to 36 million tons if routes reopen. Exports since the start of the season total only 7.2 million tons. Carryover stocks could rise to about 30 million tons by the end of 2027 if exports stay blocked.

WPIC expects the platinum market to move to a 279,000 oz deficit in 2027 after a 468,000 oz surplus in 2026. In September it expected a 265,000 oz surplus for 2026. Bar and coin demand is forecast down 28% in 2026 and up 55% in 2027. Spot platinum is down 30% year to date, its biggest annual fall since 2008.

BHP and Rio Tinto executives will meet Chinese Premier Li Qiang in Beijing on Friday as iron ore negotiations with China Mineral Resources Group (CMRG) get tougher. Singapore iron ore fell below $90 a ton to a four-year low. Goldman Sachs expects CMRG's influence on prices to grow and cut EBITDA forecasts for listed Australian miners by up to $9 billion over a decade, assuming $85-90 a ton.
Fortescue has warned operations could be affected if talks with CMRG do not conclude by year-end. The Business Council of Australia did not list Fortescue executives for the Friday roundtable.

QatarEnergy could control 175-185 mtpa of LNG, roughly a quarter of global supply, by the early 2030s according to Energy Flux. It is expanding domestic capacity to 142 mtpa from 77 mtpa and has signed long-term purchase deals with Cheniere and Woodside's US facilities. The Iran war halted Hormuz shipments and forced QatarEnergy to declare force majeure.

A 30 mtpa US LNG portfolio would lock QatarEnergy into about $4 billion a year in liquefaction fees whether or not cargoes are lifted (Energy Flux estimate). The US purchases are a financial hedge against another Hormuz closure, not a physical backup. Analysts flag buyer dependence on a single counterparty and the risk of Qatar holding more LNG than it can market.

US data centers can cut transmission costs through peak shaving. NRG says a large Texas data center can avoid $33.4 million in transmission costs by staying off the grid for one hour a year. PJM's market monitor says data center growth has added $29.4 billion to PJM system costs. Allocation rules are under regulatory review and power bills were a midterm campaign issue.
Egypt's supply ministry discussed wheat sourcing and diversification of import origins with UAE-based IRH Global Trading and Arqaam Capital. No volumes, prices or agreement were disclosed.
EU 2026/27 soft wheat exports reached 10.51 million tons by November 15, up 1% y/y. EU barley exports were 2.73 million tons, down 39% y/y.

sector_views.rationale: US LNG volumes can grow with new capacity, but rival projects in Qatar, Canada and the UAE make further share gains harder.
Goldman cut EBITDA forecasts for Australian miners by up to $9 billion over a decade as CMRG buying power grows, and iron ore is at a four-year low below $90 a ton.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A halved crop would cut supply from a major grain exporter.
Record, more than four times target, and storage is short.

risk_factors: A Middle East supply recovery would let Gulf exporters regain LNG and oil share from the US.
Continued Black Sea port closures would cut Ukraine's 2027 plantings and harvest.
Another Hormuz closure would spike gas prices and halt Qatari shipments.
CMRG's pricing power and the failure of Fortescue to reach a deal by year-end threaten iron ore miners' volumes and earnings.
India's rice surplus and subsidy costs add fiscal strain and trade friction with the US, Thailand and Vietnam.
El Nino rains could lower India's 2026/27 harvest.
geopolitical: Conflict between the US and Israel and Iran this year disrupted Middle East energy flows. An Iranian attack in March halted QatarEnergy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and forced force majeure.
Russian attacks on Black Sea terminals and ships since July blocked ports that handled 90% of Ukraine's agricultural exports. Ukraine, Turkey and India urged free navigation.

China's CMRG centralised iron ore buying and banned steelmakers from certain products from Fortescue and Rio Tinto during annual negotiations. Australia says manipulation would breach international rules.
The US accused India of dumping rice. India is negotiating a trade deal with Washington.

tension_points.bull_case: US export volumes can keep growing as new LNG facilities are commissioned and production stays near record, and the US has export flexibility across crude, LNG, NGLs and refined fuels.
tension_points.bear_case: Share gains are harder from a dominant base, and rival projects in Qatar, Canada and the UAE plus a Gulf supply recovery will take share.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Normalization of Middle East supplies and restored Gulf export flows would reduce the appeal of US barrels.

tension_points.bull_case: US purchases hedge Hormuz closure risk and would let Qatar's trading arm profit from a gas price spike, and give buyers supply security.
tension_points.bear_case: Fixed liquefaction fees of about $4 billion a year, a portfolio concentrated in Qatar and the US, and the risk of holding more LNG than it can market if Hormuz reopens.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A resolution of the Middle East crisis with Hormuz shipments back to normal would leave the US volumes hard to market.

theme_stances.key_argument: The era of easy US market-share gains is over, though export volumes can still grow with demand.
theme_stances.evidence: the era of easy gains appears to be over
